A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same macOSWorld benchmark and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-G. Corresponding content can be reliably matched, including replaced case studies and relocated figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six GUI agents, human task-completion measurements, safety outcomes, and cross-lingual and Set-of-Mark experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised UI-TARS outcomes and additional failure examples.

M1.justification: The benchmark infrastructure, task preparation, VNC action interface, programmatic evaluation, and Appendix G agent procedures remain unchanged. The revised UI-TARS results do not establish a method or model change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 202-task benchmark across 30 applications and five languages, English-only Advanced Apps evaluation, and 29-task English safety subset. Appendix D retains the same cross-lingual coverage; the replacement failure examples concern existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: The main and safety comparisons retain Claude CUA, OpenAI CUA, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, UI-TARS 7B DPO, and ShowUI 2B. Appendix D retains the OpenAI CUA language comparisons and GPT-4o comparison with and without Set-of-Mark annotations.

E3.justification: Model versions, 1024-by-768 resolution, 15-screenshot/30-dialog-turn budgets, binary success criteria, and task exclusions are unchanged. Section 5.1 simplifies the screenshot-context wording, but v1 already documents the three-screenshot policy in Appendix G; this does not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 substantially replaces the UI-TARS diagnostic evidence: v1's four grounding/planning figures and analysis of misclicks across 16 settings tasks give way to six figures examining nonsensical actions, hallucinations, and invalid outputs. Cross-lingual, Set-of-Mark, ShowUI, and CUA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports agent evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added average rows aggregate performance across languages and categories rather than introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces UI-TARS's uniformly zero success rates with nonzero results averaging 4.8% across languages. In Table 5, its Distracted/Gold/Unhandled rates change from 0.0%/0.0%/100.0% to 58.6%/34.4%/6.9%. Aggregate results and qualitative findings also change substantially, while the other agents' underlying scores and Appendix D results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same POMDP formulation, transition and reward functions, and termination horizon. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The benchmark's four principal contributions and scope remain unchanged. The abstract and introduction revise the open-source performance claim from below 2% to below 5% and the Arabic degradation from 27.5% to 28.8%, making limited changes to the headline empirical claims.

C2.justification: Sections 5.3 and E.2 replace the explanation of UI-TARS as relatively capable at planning but systematically inaccurate at grounding with an account emphasizing poor planning, hallucinations, and formatting failures. Section 5.2 places GPT-4o in the lower performance tier, and Section 5.4 now interprets UI-TARS as susceptible to deceptive pop-ups rather than predominantly leaving them unhandled.

D1.justification: The hardware, OS/application versions, prompts, generation parameters, context handling, and code/AMI access descriptions remain substantively unchanged. In particular, Appendix G.6 gives the same UI-TARS configuration despite its revised results.

R1.justification: The 48 cited works and Section 2's research positioning are unchanged. Both versions retain the same claimed gaps concerning macOS coverage, multilingual evaluation, and realistic interactive deception.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the performance and failure discussions in Sections 5.2-5.4 and Appendix E.2, with small wording edits elsewhere. The title, overall section order, benchmark exposition, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 adds per-model average rows, Table 4 becomes a compact language summary, and Table 5 changes highlighting. Table 4's individual-agent breakdown remains available in Table 3. Four UI-TARS figures are replaced by six new case-study displays, while subsequent CUA and Set-of-Mark figures are retained and renumbered or relocated.

improvement.justification: The expanded UI-TARS diagnostics are useful, but v3 introduces inconsistencies in central numerical summaries. Table 5 retains v1's 33.3% average distraction rate although the revised entries average 43.1%; its other safety averages are also stale. Table 4 reports Chinese/Japanese means of 17.2%/15.8%, whereas Table 3 implies approximately 16.7%/16.3%. These new reporting errors weaken numerical reliability and outweigh the limited diagnostic and presentation gains.
